passage: The chart on the fridge said Kamal 6, Rukmini 5. Both had homework due online by nine and only one phone. "You had it forty minutes!" "You hid the charger!" Kamal snatched the phone; Rukmini yelled "Amma!" Their mother sighed from the kitchen. "Sort it out." Kamal glared. Then the power flickered. If neither finished, both would fail. Rukmini sat on the floor. "Fine. Twenty minutes each. Timer. And a rule: no hiding chargers." Kamal exhaled. "And my room is mine when the door's shut." "Deal." They asked their mother to say yes once, out loud, so the rules would stick. She smiled. "Yes. I'll referee this one time only."

qa.q: What did the chart on the fridge say?
What was Kamal feeling when he snatched the phone and glared at his sister?
qa.a: He was annoyed and defensive, sure that he was being treated unfairly in the score they kept.

qa.q: What worked in the way Kamal and Rukmini solved the phone fight?
qa.a: They agreed on clear shared rules, a timer for each and no hiding chargers, and asked their mother to referee once so the rules would stick.

qa.q: How might Amma feel about the fighting from the kitchen?
qa.a: Probably tired and hoping they would sort it out, which is why she sighed and said she'd referee only this one time.

grounding: Shows siblings keeping score over phone and room, then agreeing shared rules and asking a parent to referee once.

passage:
Chen and his sister Valentina had been fighting since breakfast. The shared phone. The bathroom. Who got the front seat. Who Mum hugged first when she came home from her night shift at the Toronto hospital.
By evening each of them had a list. "You had the phone for two hours!" "You told Mum I broke the lamp!" "You hid my charger!"
Mum came downstairs, eyes heavy. "I'm too tired for this," she said.
Chen looked at her grey face and felt ashamed. "Okay," he said to Valentina. "Rules. Written ones."
They sat at the table with a sheet of paper. Phone: one hour each, timer on the fridge. Front seat: odd days Chen, even days Valentina. No telling tales about the lamp or anything else.
"Mum, can you check this once and be the judge?" Valentina asked. Mum read it, fixed one line, and signed it. "Once," she said, smiling tiredly. "Then it's yours to keep.

qa.q: Where did Mum work her night shift?
Why did Chen feel ashamed when Mum came downstairs?
qa.a: He felt ashamed and guilty seeing how tired she was after her night shift, realising their fighting added to her strain.
Writing clear shared rules and asking Mum to judge them once replaced the endless score-keeping with something fair they could both follow.

qa.q: How does Mum see the new rules?
qa.a: She seems relieved and willing to help once, but she wants Chen and Valentina to keep the rules themselves.

grounding: Two siblings fighting over the phone, seat and attention agree on clear shared rules and ask their mother to referee once.

passage:
The waiting room at the dental clinic was full, and the sisters had one phone between them.
"My turn," Pooja whispered.
"You've had it all morning," Rashmi hissed back. "And you told Papa I wore your jacket."
"You did wear my jacket!"
The receptionist glanced over. An old man sighed loudly.
Pooja kept a list in her head: the jacket, the bigger cupboard, the time Papa took Rashmi alone for ice cream. Rashmi kept her own. Each round was louder than the last.
Rashmi finally grabbed a clinic token slip and a pen. "Enough. Let's write it down properly."
They scribbled on the back: Phone, thirty minutes each, alarm set. Cupboard, swap every term. Clothes, ask first. No running to Papa unless it's serious.
When Papa came out, numb-lipped, they held it up. "Can you check it? Just this once." He read it twice, nodded, and stuck it in his wallet.

qa.q: Where did the sisters write their rules?
qa.a: On the back of a clinic token slip.

qa.q: What was Pooja feeling as the arguments kept getting louder?
qa.a: Pooja felt resentful and competitive, keeping a mental list of every unfair thing she believed Rashmi had got.

qa.q: What small step helped the sisters, and why?
qa.a: Writing clear shared rules and asking Papa to check them once stopped the endless scorekeeping.

qa.q: How might Papa see the rules when they hold them up?
qa.a: Papa probably feels surprised and relieved that the sisters solved it themselves, and he keeps the slip as proof of the deal.

grounding: Two sisters fighting and keeping score agree on clear shared rules and ask their father to referee them once.
